STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r20.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r20.claim: Verses 104–126 give one of the Quran's most detailed accounts of Moses confronting Pharaoh and the sorcerers.
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r20.anchor:
most
detailed accounts of Moses’ confrontation with Pharaoh and the sorcerers (vv. 104–26)

BURSEVI:v3p161#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p161#4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p161#4/r2.claim: He threatens to cut off each person’s right hand and left foot, then crucify all of them on date-palm trunks beside the Nile to disgrace and deter others.
BURSEVI:v3p161#4/r2.anchor: {لاقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف} أي : من كل شق طرفا

BURSEVI:v3p161#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p161#4/r3.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v3p161#4/r3.claim: It is said Pharaoh first instituted crucifixion, after which God prescribed it for highway robbers because their crime is so grave.
BURSEVI:v3p161#4/r3.anchor: قيل : هو أول من سن ذلك فشرعه الله تعالى لقطاع الطريق

SULAMI:v1p235#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p235#3/r1.speaker: سمنون
SULAMI:v1p235#3/r1.claim: Those present in direct witnessing can bear afflictions that they could not bear in its absence; Pharaoh's magicians ignored his threat.
SULAMI:v1p235#3/r1.anchor: قال سمنون : يحمل الهياكل من البلايا على المشاهدة ما لا تحمله في حال الغيبة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1537#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1537#3/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1537#3/r1.claim: Pharaoh was the first to cut hands and feet crosswise and crucify people.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1537#3/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير لاقطعن ايديكم وارجلكم من خلاف ثم لاصلبنكم وكان اول من قطع الايدي والارجل وصلب فرعون .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1537#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1537#3/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1537#3/r2.claim: Pharaoh carried out the threat, killing and cutting their limbs.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1537#3/r2.anchor: عن السدى لاقطعن ايديكم وارجلكم من خلاف فقتلهم وقطعهم كما قال .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p54#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p54#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p54#2/r1.claim: The object of Pharaoh's threat, what the magicians would come to know, is omitted to make the threat terrifying; the definite plural covers every hand and foot of every sorcerer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p54#2/r1.anchor: وحذف مفعول { تعلمون } لقصد الإجمال في الوعيد لإدخال الرعب ، ثم بينه بجملة { لأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p54#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p54#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p54#2/r2.claim: Min khilaf identifies opposite sides: each sorcerer loses one hand and the opposite foot, leaving the person able to walk or lean on a stick.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p54#2/r2.anchor: أنه يقطع من كل ساحر يدا ورجلا متخالفتي الجهة غير متقابلتيها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p54#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p54#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p54#2/r3.claim: If crucifixion means killing on a cross, the threat names two alternative punishments for different groups; cutting first then killing would make the crosswise detail pointless.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p54#2/r3.anchor: موجه إلى جماعتهم فعلم أنه جعلهم فريقين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p54#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p54#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p54#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, crucifixion may mean suspension without killing after amputation, as a public warning; then thumma signals a delay for healing, and all are crucified.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p54#2/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن يراد بالصلب : الصلب دون قتل ، فيكون أراد صلبهم بعد القطع ليجعلهم نكالا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p54#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p54#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p54#2/r5.claim: The magicians' reply that they return to God answers that Pharaoh's threat cannot harm them; they hope for God's reward and forgiveness and for punishment of Pharaoh, or welcome martyrdom and meeting God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p54#2/r5.anchor: وعيد لا يضيرهم ، لأنهم يعلمون أنهم صائرون إلى الله رب الجميع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440/r9.speaker: حميد المكي وابن محصن ومجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440/r9.claim: They read the threat with alternate vocalization of the verbs for cutting and crucifying; another report gives a kasra on the lām of the latter verb.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440/r9.anchor: وقرأ حميد المكي وابن محصن ومجاهد «لأقطعن» بفتح الهمزة والطاء وإسكان القاف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440/r10.claim: Min khilāf means the right hand with the left foot and the left hand with the right foot.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#2/r1.claim: The verses state Pharaoh’s threat but do not say he carried it out; reports say he cut and crucified some, while the threat applied to all.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#2/r1.anchor: والظاهر من هذه الآيات أن فرعون توعد وليس في القرآن نص على أنه أنفذ ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Pharaoh was the first to crucify and amputate crosswise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فرعون أول من صلب وقطع من خلاف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#2/r3.claim: They say the converts were sorcerers in the morning and martyrs by evening.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p440#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وغيره فيهم: أصبحوا سحرة وأمسوا شهداء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p243/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p243/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p243/r1.claim: “Crosswise” means the right hand and left leg are cut off.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p243/r1.anchor: وهو قطع اليد اليمنى والرجل اليسر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p243/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p243/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p243/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Pharaoh was the first to carry out cross-amputation and the first to crucify.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p243/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس أول من فعل ذلك وأول من صلب فرعون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p458#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p458#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p458#2/r1.claim: Pharaoh accuses the magicians of conspiring with Moses to seize power, expel the leaders, and control the city, then says they will see what he does to them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p458#2/r1.anchor: أي: تجتمعوا أنتم وهو، وتكون لكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p458#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p458#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p458#2/r2.claim: Pharaoh threatens to cut each person's opposite hand and foot and crucify them all; the parallel wording says they would be crucified on palm trunks.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p458#2/r2.anchor: يعني: يقطع يد الرجل اليمنى ورجله اليسرى أو بالعكس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p458#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p458#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p458#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Pharaoh was the first to crucify people and to cut hands and feet on opposite sides.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p458#2/r3.anchor: أول من صلب، وأول من قطع الأيدي والأرجل من خلاف، فرعون

JISHUMI:v4p2675/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2675/r2.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v4p2675/r2.claim: The common reading has tanqimū with kasra on the qāf; al-Hasan uses fatḥa, and both forms express taking vengeance or punishing.
JISHUMI:v4p2675/r2.anchor: وظاهر القراءة ما تنقم بكسر القاف، وعن الحسن بفتحها، وهما لغتان

JISHUMI:v4p2675/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2675/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2675/r3.claim: Taqṭīʿ means multiplying cuts; ṣalb is binding to wood, and inqilāb is returning, derived from turning back.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p133#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p133#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p133#2/r1.claim: A declarative reading of ‘Have you believed him?’ rebukes the magicians; an interrogative reading expresses denial and incredulity.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p133#2/r1.anchor: ءامنتم به } على الإخبار ، أي فعلتم هذا الفعل الشنيع ، توبيخا لهم وتقريعا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p133#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p133#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p133#2/r2.claim: Pharaoh alleges that Moses and the magicians conspired in Egypt before the exodus to expel the Copts and settle Israelites, as propaganda against their conversion.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p133#2/r2.anchor: إن صنعكم هذا لحيلة احتلتموها أنتم وموسى في مصر قبل أن تخرجوا إلى هذه الصحراء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p133#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p133#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p133#2/r3.claim: A report says Moses asked the chief magician whether he would believe if defeated; the magician promised to believe if his unbeatable magic lost, and Pharaoh heard.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p133#2/r3.anchor: وروي أن موسى عليه السلام قال للساحر الأكبر : أتؤمن بي إن غلبتك ؟ قال : لآتين بسحر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p133#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p133#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p133#2/r4.claim: Pharaoh’s general threat is specified by cutting and crucifixion; readings lighten the lām in both verbs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p133#2/r4.anchor: وعيد أجمله ثم فصله بقوله : { لاقطعن } وقرىء : ( لأقطعن ) بالتخفيف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p133#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p133#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p133#2/r5.claim: Cutting ‘from opposite sides’ means taking a limb from each opposing side of the body.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p133#2/r5.anchor: { من خلاف } من كل شق طرفا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p133#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p133#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p133#2/r6.claim: It is said Pharaoh was the first to cut and crucify people crosswise.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p133#2/r6.anchor: وقيل : إن أول من قطع من خلاف وصلب لفرعون

MUQATIL:7:124-129/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:124-129/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:124-129/r1.claim: Pharaoh threatens to cut off opposite limbs, the right hand and left foot or left hand and right foot, then crucify all the magicians.
MUQATIL:7:124-129/r1.anchor: يعنى اليد اليمنى والرجل اليسرى، أو الرجل اليمنى واليد اليسرى،

NASAFI-FULL:v2p30#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p30#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p30#7/r1.claim: Cutting hands and feet crosswise means taking one limb from each side; Pharaoh was the first to use this punishment and crucify its victims.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p30#7/r1.anchor: هو أول من قطع من خلاف وصلب

RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r1.claim: Pharaoh's threat means cutting a hand and the opposite foot, either right hand with left foot or left hand with right, then crucifying all of them.
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r1.anchor: وقطع اليد والرجل من خلاف معروف المعنى ، وهو أن يقطعهما من جهتين مختلفتين

RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r2.claim: The verse itself does not show whether Pharaoh carried out the threat.
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r2.anchor: واختلفوا في أنه هل وقع ذلك منه ؟ وليس في الآية ما يدل على أحد الأمرين .

RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r3.claim: One argument for execution is that Pharaoh's officials later warn about Moses and his people, but the reply is that the magicians were subsumed under “his people.”
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r3.anchor: واحتج بعضهم على وقوعه بوجوه : الأول : أنه تعالى حكى عن الملأ من قوم فرعون أنهم قالوا له : { أتذر موسى وقومه ليفسدوا فى الارض }

RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Pharaoh carried out the cross-amputation; the author calls this the more apparent account, as a warning to deter others from Moses' religion.
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r5.anchor: الثالث : ما نقل عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه أنه فعل ذلك وقطع أيديهم وأرجلهم من خلاف ، وهذا هو الأظهر

RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r6.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r6.claim: Others say the threat was not carried out and God answered their prayer to die Muslims, meaning their death came from God rather than execution; the author calls this inference close.
RAZI-FULL:v14p170/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون : إنه لم يقع من فرعون ذلك ، بل استجاب الله تعالى لهم الدعاء في قولهم : { وتوفنا مسلمين } لأنهم سألوه تعالى أن يكون توفيهم من جهته

SAMIN-DURR:7:124/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:124/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:124/r1.claim: The threat is placed in an oath-like sentence for emphasis.
SAMIN-DURR:7:124/r1.anchor: لأقطعن } جاء به في جملة قسمية تأكيدا لما يفعله

SAMIN-DURR:7:124/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:124/r2.speaker: مجاهد بن جبر
SAMIN-DURR:7:124/r2.claim: Mujahid, Humayd al-Makki, and Ibn Muhaysin lighten لأقطعن and ولأصلبنكم, reading the triliteral forms; صلب also has both vowel patterns in the imperfect.
SAMIN-DURR:7:124/r2.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد بن جبر وحميد المكي وابن محيصن: " لأقطعن " مخففا من قطع الثلاثي

SAMIN-DURR:7:124/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:124/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:124/r3.claim: من خلاف may mean cutting a limb from opposite sides, conventionally the right hand and left foot; grammatically it is circumstantial.
SAMIN-DURR:7:124/r3.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون المعنى: على أنه يقطع من كل شق طرفا فيقطع اليد اليمنى والرجل اليسرى

SAMIN-DURR:7:124/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:124/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:124/r4.claim: Alternatively من is causal, meaning the punishment is for their opposition, though attaching it directly to the verb is remote.
SAMIN-DURR:7:124/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المعنى: لأقطعن لأجل مخالفتكم إياي فتكون " من " تعليلية

SAMIN-DURR:7:124/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:124/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:124/r5.claim: أجمعين is emphatic even without the usual preceding كل.
SAMIN-DURR:7:124/r5.anchor: وأجمعين تأكيد، أي به دون " كل " وإن كان الأكثر سبقه ب كل

SAMIN-DURR:7:124/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:124/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:124/r6.claim: ثم here does not conflict with the waw in the parallel passages because waw can also allow a time interval.
SAMIN-DURR:7:124/r6.anchor: وجيء هنا ب " ثم " وفي السورتين " ولأصلبنكم " بالواو، لأن الواو صالحة للمهلة

STUDYQURAN:7:111/r37.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r37.speaker: Th
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r37.claim: Pharaoh's warning that they will soon know refers to the terrible punishment he plans to impose.
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r37.anchor: that is, they will know the terrible punishment Pharaoh intends to impose on them (Th)

STUDYQURAN:7:111/r38.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r38.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r38.claim: Pharaoh's threatened punishment resembles the penalty for waging war against God and His Messenger and spreading corruption.
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r38.anchor: The punishment here is similar to the punishment ordained for those who wage war against God and His Messenger and endeavor to work corruption upon the earth

STUDYQURAN:7:111/r39.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r39.speaker: Q, Ṭs, Z
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r39.claim: Commentators report Pharaoh was the first to impose cutting opposite hands and feet followed by crucifixion.
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r39.anchor: The commentators report that the first person to execute the punishment of “cutting off hands and feet on alternate sides” and crucifixion was Pharaoh

STUDYQURAN:7:111/r40.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r40.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r40.claim: Pharaoh crucified victims on palm trees beside the Nile; the threat's parallel in 20:71 mentions this detail.
STUDYQURAN:7:111/r40.anchor: who crucified his victims on palm trees on the banks of the Nile (Ṭs)

TAB-FULL:v10p363#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p363#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p363#2/r1.claim: Crosswise amputation means cutting one hand and the opposite foot, either right hand with left foot or left hand with right foot; crosswise means the two limbs are on opposite sides.
TAB-FULL:v10p363#2/r1.anchor: ورجله اليمنى، فيخالف بين العضوين في القطع، فمخالفته في ذلك بينهما هو القطع من خلاف.

TAB-FULL:v10p363#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p363#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p363#2/r2.claim: Pharaoh threatens crucifixion after seeing God abandon him and Moses overcome him.
TAB-FULL:v10p363#2/r2.anchor: وإنما قال هذا فرعون، لما رأى من خذلان الله إياه وغلبة موسى عليه السلام وقهره له

TAB-FULL:v10p363#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p363#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p363#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says Pharaoh was the first to crucify and to amputate hands and feet crosswise.
TAB-FULL:v10p363#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {لأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف ثم لأصلبنكم أجمعين} [الأعراف: 124] قال: أول من صلب وأول من قطع الأيدي والأرجل من خلاف فرعون "

TABATABAI:7:122-124/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:122-124/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:122-124/r5.claim: Pharaoh threatens first to cut opposite limbs, meaning one hand and the opposite foot, then to crucify them by fastening them to raised wood as a public warning.
TABATABAI:7:122-124/r5.anchor: وهو أن يقطع اليد اليمنى مع الرجل اليسرى أو اليد اليسرى مع الرجل اليمنى

TABRISI:7:123-126/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:123-126/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:123-126/r2.claim: Pharaoh accuses the magicians of conspiring with Moses in the city to drive out its people; he aims to deceive the crowd into thinking their belief is a political plot rather than recognition of truth.
TABRISI:7:123-126/r2.anchor: أراد فرعون بهذا القول التلبيس على الناس وإيهامهم أن إيمان السحرة لم يكن عن علم

TABRISI:7:123-126/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:123-126/r3.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:7:123-126/r3.claim: An alternative says the magicians arranged the plan with Moses in Egypt before coming, intending to take over Egypt and expel its people.
TABRISI:7:123-126/r3.anchor: وقيل: معناه إن هذا لصنيع صنعتموه فيما بينكم وبين موسى في مصر

TABRISI:7:123-126/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:123-126/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:123-126/r4.claim: Pharaoh’s threat to cut hands and feet crosswise means taking opposite-side limbs; al-Ḥasan specifies right hand with left foot or left hand with right foot.
TABRISI:7:123-126/r4.anchor: قال الحسن: هو أن يقطع اليد اليمنى مع الرجل اليسرى وكذلك اليد اليسرى

TABRISI:7:123-126/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:123-126/r5.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:7:123-126/r5.claim: A report says Pharaoh was the first to amputate and crucify, fastening them to date-palm trunks along the Nile in Egypt.
TABRISI:7:123-126/r5.anchor: وقيل: إن أول من قطع الرجل وصلب فرعون صلبهم في جذوع النخل

TABRISI:7:123-126/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:123-126/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:123-126/r8.claim: Crucifixion derives from fastening someone to wood and all Qurʾānic readers double its lām; na-qima can mean punish or object, while “punishment” contrasts with a blameworthy injury. Ifrāgh is pouring out, and ṣabr is restraining visible despair; patience for truth is honor.
TABRISI:7:123-126/r8.anchor: الصلب الشد على الخشبة وغيرها وأصله من صلابة الشيء والقراء كلهم على تشديد اللام

THALABI:v4p270/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p270/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p270/r7.claim: Pharaoh’s threat means cutting limbs on opposite sides, then crucifying all of them on the bank of the Nile in Egypt.
THALABI:v4p270/r7.anchor: لأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف وهو أن يقطع من شق طرفا

THALABI:v4p270/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p270/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v4p270/r8.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says Pharaoh was the first to cut people’s limbs crosswise.
THALABI:v4p270/r8.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: أول من قطع من خلاف فرعون

ASAD-NOTES:7:120#n92/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:120#n92/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:120#n92/r1.claim: The Arabic verb forms indicate Pharaoh threatened to cut off and crucify the sorcerers in great numbers, meaning either the converts were numerous or had many followers.
ASAD-NOTES:7:120#n92/r1.anchor: either the repentant sorcerers thus addressed were many or, alternatively, that they had a large following

ASAD-NOTES:7:120#n92/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:120#n92/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:120#n92/r2.claim: The possibility of a large following is supported by the Biblical report that many Egyptians joined Israel’s exodus.
ASAD-NOTES:7:120#n92/r2.anchor: many Egyptians joined the Israelites in their exodus from Egypt: "And a mixed multitude went up also with them"

ASAD-NOTES:7:120#n92/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:120#n92/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:120#n92/r3.claim: Asad’s rendering of min khilaf as “because of perverseness” is explained in his note on 5:33.
ASAD-NOTES:7:120#n92/r3.anchor: As regards my rendering of min khilaf as "because of [your] perverseness", see surah 5, note 44

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288/r1.claim: The verb of cutting is intensive because the verse refers to plural hands.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288/r1.anchor: استعمل لفظ التقطيع هاهنا لمكان الأيدي وهي جمع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288/r2.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288/r2.claim: Min khilāf means cutting opposite-side limbs, such as the right hand and left leg.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288/r2.anchor: يقطع من كل شق طرف كاليد اليمنى مع الرجل اليسرى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p288/r3.claim: Pharaoh was the first to carry out this form of amputation.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:123-125/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:123-125/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:123-125/r2.claim: Crosswise cutting means severing one limb from each opposite side.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:123-125/r2.anchor: وهو أن يقطع من كل شق طرف

ELMALILI:7:117-125#6/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:117-125#6/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:117-125#6/r9.claim: After the magicians' public defeat and conversion, Pharaoh claimed the event was a plot and threatened to cut their opposite limbs and crucify them all.
ELMALILI:7:117-125#6/r9.anchor: ellerinizi ve ayaklarınızı çaprazına kestireceğim, sonra da hepinizi elbette ve elbette çarmıha gerdireceğim

ELMALILI:7:117-125#6/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:117-125#6/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:117-125#6/r10.claim: Had the magicians' faith been a deceitful collusion, Pharaoh's threat would have stopped them; sincere believers instead grow firmer in their resolve against injustice.
ELMALILI:7:117-125#6/r10.anchor: kalbleri mahabbetullah ile çarpan ve âhirete cidden iman

ELMALILI:7:117-125#6/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:117-125#6/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:117-125#6/r11.claim: Because the magicians were known for skill in magic, suspicion about their sincerity was not wholly groundless; public testing removed that doubt.
ELMALILI:7:117-125#6/r11.anchor: Sâhirler mukaddemâ sihirde maharetle mâruf kimseler olduklarından dolayı imanlarında böyle bir mekr ü hile şüphesi büsbütün sebepsiz addolunamazdı

ELMALILI:7:117-125#6/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:117-125#6/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:117-125#6/r12.claim: Divine wisdom required the magicians to prove publicly and decisively that their faith was sincere and that Moses' miracle was not magic.
ELMALILI:7:117-125#6/r12.anchor: Allah teâlâ kendilerini hakk u halk muvâcehesinde böyle bir imtihâna tâbi‘tuttu ve muvaffak kıldı

ELMALILI:7:117-125#6/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:117-125#6/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:117-125#6/r13.claim: The magicians' response that they would return to their Lord can mean that death is inevitable whether Pharaoh kills them or not, so his threat is powerless.
ELMALILI:7:117-125#6/r13.anchor: Biz nasıl olsa öleceğiz, sen istesen de öleceğiz istemesen de

ELMALILI:7:117-125#6/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:117-125#6/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:117-125#6/r14.claim: Their response can also mean that execution would make them martyrs who reach their Lord's mercy and reward, so they welcome dying for truth.
ELMALILI:7:117-125#6/r14.anchor: Sen bizi keser, asarsan biz şehid olur ve muhakkak Rabbimizin rahmet ü sevâbına kavuşuruz

ELMALILI:7:117-125#7/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:117-125#7/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:117-125#7/r1.claim: A third possible meaning is that Pharaoh and the magicians will all die and stand before their Lord, who will judge between oppressor and oppressed.
ELMALILI:7:117-125#7/r1.anchor: gerek biz ve gerek sen hepimiz ölüp Rabbimizin

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:123/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:123/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:123/r1.claim: The magicians had openly believed in Moses, so Pharaoh's words about believing without his permission are a threat, not a question; his promised punishments make this clear.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:123/r1.anchor: sözü, bir soru olmayıp tehditten ibarettir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:123/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:123/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:123/r2.claim: Pharaoh's claim that they needed his permission to believe shows he asserted control over all their behavior and beliefs and suppressed their consciences.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:123/r2.anchor: onların her türlü tutum ve davranışlarına hükmettiğini, vicdanlarını baskı altında tuttuğunu göstermektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:123/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:123/r3.speaker: Fahreddin er-Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:123/r3.claim: Razi says the public defeat caused political anxiety: Pharaoh feared the people would follow the magicians and Moses, so he alleged a prior conditional agreement and trap to discredit Moses' victory; his unspoken concern was losing unpaid labor.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:123/r3.anchor: Fahreddin er-Râzî’ye göre Firavun’un Mûsâ karşısındaki bu yenilgisi, onda aynı zamanda siyasî bir endişe de doğurdu

ALUSI-FULL:v9p27#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p27#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p27#2/r1.claim: Cutting hands and feet 'from opposite sides' means taking a hand from one side and a foot from the other; min is circumstantial, while explaining it causally as punishment for opposition is remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p27#2/r1.anchor: كاليد من جانب والرجل من آخر والجار في موضع الحال

ALUSI-FULL:v9p27#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p27#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p27#2/r2.claim: Pharaoh threatens crucifixion of all as public disgrace and deterrence; salb originally means binding to wood and came to mean hanging someone by the neck until death.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p27#2/r2.anchor: تفضيحا لكم وتنكيلا لأمثالكم والتصليب مأخوذ من الصلب وهو الشد على خشبة أو غيرها

ALUSI-FULL:v9p27#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p27#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v9p27#2/r3.claim: An Ibn Abbas report says Pharaoh's crucifixion was binding a person under the arms and hanging him until death, a punishment he first introduced, as he did amputation.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p27#2/r3.anchor: أن الصلب الذي عناه الجبار هو شد الشخص من تحت الإبطين وتعليقه حتى يهلك وهو كقطع الأيدي والأرجل أول من سنه فرعون

ALUSI-FULL:v9p27#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p27#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p27#2/r4.claim: God prescribed crucifixion for highway robbers because their crime is grave, hence describing it as war against God and His messenger.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p27#2/r4.anchor: وشرعه الله تعالى لقطاع الطريق تعظيما لجرمهم ولهذا سماه سبحانه محاربة لله ولرسوله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p266/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p266/r5.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p266/r5.claim: Cutting them crosswise means the right hand and left foot; Pharaoh threatens to crucify them all on the bank of the Nile in Egypt.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p266/r5.anchor: قال الكلبي: لأقطعن أيديكم اليمنى وأرجلكم اليسرى، {ثم لأصلبنكم أجمعين} على شاطئ [نهر] (1) مصر.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:124/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:124/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:124/r1.claim: Min khilāf means cutting opposite-side hands and feet; crucifixion publicly disgraces offenders and deters others.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:124/r1.anchor: من كل شق طرفا. { ثم لأصلبنكم أجمعين } تفضيحا لكم وتنكيلا لأمثالكم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:124/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:124/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:124/r2.claim: An opinion says Pharaoh first instituted crucifixion and God prescribed it for highway robbers, magnifying their crime as warfare against God and His messenger; the penalty is understood sequentially from divine mercy.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:124/r2.anchor: قيل إنه أول من سن ذلك فشرعه الله للقطاع تعظميا لجرمهم ولذلك سماه محاربة لله ورسوله

BIQAI-FULL:v3p83/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p83/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p83/r9.claim: Pharaoh threatens opposite-side amputation, then crucifixion; the delayed “then” lengthens the threat to frighten the magicians and wavering onlookers, and crucifixion may mean a cross-shaped display or torture until bodily fluid runs.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p83/r9.anchor: ولما كان مقصود هذه السورة الإنذار , فذكر فيها ما وقع لموسى عليه السلام والسحرة على وجه يهول

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r2.claim: Thumma indicates delay, so al-Aʿrāf gives the magicians respite before crucifixion; Shuʿarāʾ has no respite, matching Pharaoh’s hotter anger.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r2.anchor: و (ثم) تفيد التراخي، ولم يُعطهم مهلة في الشعراء

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r3.claim: The magicians’ added no harm in Shuʿarāʾ suits both that account’s fuller detail and its more severe threat.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r3.anchor: فزاد (لا ضير) في الشعراء وهو المناسب لمقام التفصيل من ناحية

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r4.claim: Their fearlessness under Shuʿarāʾ’s greater threat shows they feared the lesser threat in al-Aʿrāf even less; saying it only there could imply otherwise.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r4.anchor: من المعتاد أن يرهب الإنسان التهديد الكبير دون الصغير

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r5.claim: Stating their fearlessness under the greater threat entails it under the lesser one, so the stronger-scene statement covers both by a fortiori reasoning.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r5.anchor: إن ذكره في موطن التهديد الكبير يغني عن ذكره في الموطن الأدنى

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r6.claim: Repeating no harm in both accounts would impair concision; Shuʿarāʾ is built for detail, while al-Aʿrāf is summarized.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r6.anchor: ثم إن ذكره في الموطنين مخل بالإيجاز

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r7.claim: The accounts pursue different narrative paths: al-Aʿrāf recounts Israel’s history, signs, sins, and ingratitude; Shuʿarāʾ moves to Pharaoh’s end and Israel’s rescue.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r7.anchor: فيمضي في الأعراف لذكره أحوال بني إسرائيل وتاريخهم والآليات التي أروها ومعاصيهم واستهانتهم بالنعم والآليات

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r8.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r8.claim: Each account places the expression suited to its distinct scene; the wording choices deliberately serve the fine artistic design.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16#3/r8.anchor: اختيار الألفاظ والعبارات كان مقصوداً لخدمة الناحية الفنية في أدق معانيها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p747/r9.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p747/r9.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p747/r9.claim: The wording contrasts ولأصلبنكم in Al Shu'ara with ثم لأصلبنكم in Al A'raf.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p749/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p749/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p749/r7.claim: ثم in Al A'raf indicates Pharaoh gave the sorcerers a respite, while the Shu'ara wording shows none.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p749/r7.anchor: وهذا يدل على أنه أعطاهم مهلة في سورة الأعراف ولم يعطهم مهلة في سورة الشعراء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p223#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p223#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p223#2/r2.claim: Thumma retains its ordinary sense of sequence and interval in many passages.
